messages.subject: Need up-to-date world maps for ggplot2 ('maps package > old data)
parts:

Maria

messages.author: d3aaa07872b9962c
messages.subject: Re: Need up-to-date world maps for ggplot2 ('maps package > old data)
parts:
Data in R-packages is just examples or proof of concept, don't expect it to be up-to-date or comprehensive. I suggest you download data separately and use an R-package to read that data.

For a world map, see e.g. Natural Earth.
http://www.naturalearthdata.com/

Map data is usually available as shapefiles, which you can read with readOGR from the rgdal package. To plot the map with ggplot2, you'll need to call fortify to convert from the sp object to a data frame.

https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/plotting-polygon-shapefiles

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: Need up-to-date world maps for ggplot2 ('maps package > old data)
parts:
I like having the control of specifying my own shape files  (like Osmo suggested with Natural Earth).    But the `rworldmap` package (http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rworldmap/) seems to have an up-to-date information.  It seems like they could benefit from a vignette example how to use the data with ggplot/ggmap.  I'm sure you can figure it out with some time, but there are so many different variations & potential conversions of spatial formats.

Without a ggplot/ggmap vignette example from rworldmap, it's probably quicker to import a Natural Earth shape file.  It's a shame, because it's probably less than 8 lines of code to convert the rworldmap information, and then your script is portable to any computer than can install the package.

messages.author: e5d0b3c2486cd4e3
messages.subject: Re: Need up-to-date world maps for ggplot2 ('maps package > old data)
parts:
I actually wrote a wrapper a few months back to data(wrld_simpl) in the maptools package. I think it's the same as the map in rworldmap.


suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(maptools)
  library(ggplot2)
})



PolygonCoords <- function(polygon) {
  polygons <- polygon@Polygons
  coords.list <- lapply(seq_along(polygons), function(i) {
    # Extract the group, sequence, area, longitude, and latitude.
    coords <- polygons[[i]]@coords
    cbind(i, 1:nrow(coords), polygons[[i]]@area, coords)
  })
  coords.df <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, coords.list))
  names(coords.df) <- c("order", "seq", "area", "long", "lat")
  return(coords.df)
}

ConvertWorldSimple <- function(mapdata, min.area = 0) {

  # min.area is the minimum size of the polygons. Setting to some  # positive value will filter out tiny islands.


  coords.list <- lapply(mapdata@polygons, PolygonCoords)
  ncoords <- sapply(coords.list, nrow)
  coords.df <- do.call(rbind, coords.list)
  coords.df$country <- rep(mapdata@data$NAME, ncoords)
  country.group <- factor(paste(coords.df$country, coords.df$order))
  coords.df$group <- as.numeric(country.group)
  coords.df <- coords.df[coords.df$area >= min.area, ]
  return(coords.df)
}

data("wrld_simpl")
world <- ConvertWorldSimple(wrld_simpl, min.area = 0.1)


# Now do something interesting with the map. Be careful, though,# merging screws up the order of the polygons.
na <- data.frame(
  country = c("United States", "Canada", "Mexico"),
  is.north.america = TRUE)
world <- merge(world, na, all.x = TRUE)
world$is.north.america[is.na(world$is.north.america)] <- FALSE

# Let's fix the order now. This is why we saved the 'seq' with the data.
world <- world[order(world$order, world$seq), ]

ggplot(world, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(aes(fill = is.north.america)) +
  geom_path(color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkgray", "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous("", breaks=(-2:2) * 30) +
  scale_x_continuous("", breaks=(-4:4) * 45) +
  coord_equal() +  theme_bw()

messages.author: 61cea80f29d13218
messages.subject: Re: Need up-to-date world maps for ggplot2 ('maps package > old data)
parts:
Hi there, 
Here is a simple example using ggplot2 for geographical data (from Buenos Aires, Argentina). 
I believe there are many examples using the World, USA but not much more from other countries.
You can use gadm.org to download the spatial poligons data frame (they have it set for use in R).
take care

library(ggplot2); library(plyr);
df <- data.frame(long = c(-58.1, -58.2, -58.3, -58.4, -58.5, -55),
                 lat = c(-34.1, -34.2, -34.3, -34.4, -34.5, -25))
con <- url("http://gadm.org/data/rda/ARG_adm2.RData")
print(load(con))
close(con)

ggmap <- fortify(gadm, region = "NAME_2")  
ggplot(data=ggmap, aes(x=long, y=lat)) +
    geom_polygon(data=ggmap, fill="grey80", aes(group=group)) +
    geom_path(color="white",aes(group=group)) +
    geom_point(data=df, aes(x=long, y=lat), colour="red", alpha=30/100) +
    coord_map(xlim=-c(59, 58), ylim=-c(35,34))



2013/11/14 Sundar Dorai-Raj <sdor...@gmail.com>

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: Need up-to-date world maps for ggplot2 ('maps package > old data)
parts:
Sundar, I'm glad people like you and Gotan have taken the time to figure it out for others like us.  Thank you.  

Consider replacing the North American merging code with this code.  Two versions are equivalent, but this approach may be easier to build additional layers on top of it.

world$is.north.america <- (world$country %in% c("United States", "Canada", "Mexico")) 

(And there are five or six other North American countries that might be visible at your scale: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_North_American_countries_by_population)
